species.name: Billfish
species.quote: Billfish (Blue marlin, White marlin, Sailfish)* | Billfish may be landed in Georgia, provided the angler complies with all federal regulations. Visit CoastalGaDNR.org/HMS for federal regulations.
species.notes: Georgia prints no state season, size or bag; defers entirely to federal HMS rules. CoastalGaDNR.org/HMS links to https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/topic/atlantic-highly-migratory-species/overview

zones.label: GA state waters (to 3 nm)
zones.bagNote: Federal HMS rules apply — no separate Georgia limit

zones.label: Federal waters (3–200 nm)
zones.bagNote: Federal HMS rules apply

userNotes: Georgia sets no state limit on blue marlin, white marlin or sailfish — you may land them in Georgia only if you follow all federal HMS rules (permit, sizes, reporting).
Check NOAA Atlantic HMS regulations before keeping any billfish: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/topic/atlantic-highly-migratory-species/overview

species.name: Hammerhead Sharks
species.quote: Hammerhead Sharks (Great, Scalloped, and Smooth)A | 78 FL
species.season: All year (printed in the shark block with 'Sharks (other than Hammerheads, SSC and Prohibited Sharks)' — 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less)
species.limit: 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less
species.notes: Printed as a sub-row of the Sharks block; the limit column is merged with the 'Sharks (other than ...)' row above it. Footnote A: also federally managed — see NOAA HMS. Sharks: hook and line only; non-offset, corrodible, non-stainless circle hooks required except with flies/artificial lures. Must be landed with head and fins intact.

zones.label: GA state waters (to 3 nm)
zones.bagNote: 1 shark per angler or per boat, whichever is less (shared with all other non-SSC sharks)

zones.label: Federal waters (3–200 nm)
zones.bagNote: Federal HMS rules apply — see NOAA
zones.sizeNote: Federal HMS minimum size applies (78 inch FL)

userNotes: Great, scalloped and smooth hammerheads must be at least 78 inches fork length — much bigger than the 54-inch rule for other sharks.
Only one shark (of any non-small-shark-composite species) per angler or per boat, whichever is less.
Hook and line only, with non-offset non-stainless circle hooks unless using flies or artificial lures. Land the shark with head and fins intact.
Federal rules also apply: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/atlantic-highly-migratory-species/atlantic-highly-migratory-species-minimum-sizes-and-bag-limits

species.name: Shortfin Mako Shark
species.quote: Shortfin Mako Shark | When Federal Quota is Available. | 83 FL
species.limit: 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less
species.notes: Printed in the Sharks block; limit column merged with 'Sharks (other than ...)'. CRD page prints '54" FL (83" FL for Shortfin Makos)'. Longfin mako is a prohibited species.

zones.label: GA state waters (to 3 nm)
zones.bagNote: 1 per angler or boat, whichever is less — only when the federal shortfin mako retention quota is open

zones.label: Federal waters (3–200 nm)
zones.bagNote: Federal HMS rules apply — retention only when NOAA opens the quota

userNotes: Shortfin mako can only be kept when NOAA has the federal retention quota open — assume it is closed unless you have confirmed on the NOAA HMS site.
Minimum 83 inches fork length; one shark per angler or boat, whichever is less.
Longfin mako looks similar and is PROHIBITED — if in doubt, release.

species.name: Prohibited Sharks
species.quote: Prohibited Sharks (NO HARVEST)A | Sand tiger, Sandbar, Silky, Bigeye sand tiger, Whale, Basking, White, Dusky, Bignose, Galapagos, Night, Reef, Narrowtooth, Caribbean sharpnose, Smalltail, Atlantic angel, Longfin mako, Bigeye thresher, Sharpnose sevengill, Bluntnose sixgill, Oceanic Whitetip, and Bigeye sixgill
species.notes: 22 species listed. Footnote A: also federally managed. 'Most sharks with an interdorsal ridge caught in Georgia waters will be included in the “prohibited” or “no harvest” categories.' (saltwater fish ID page)

zones.label: GA state waters (to 3 nm)
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

zones.label: Federal waters (3–200 nm)
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

userNotes: No harvest of any of these 22 shark species in Georgia: sand tiger, sandbar, silky, bigeye sand tiger, whale, basking, white, dusky, bignose, Galapagos, night, reef, narrowtooth, Caribbean sharpnose, smalltail, Atlantic angel, longfin mako, bigeye thresher, sharpnose sevengill, bluntnose sixgill, oceanic whitetip, bigeye sixgill.
Most ridge-backed sharks (an interdorsal ridge between the dorsal fins) caught off Georgia are prohibited. If you are not sure of the species, release it.

species.name: Largemouth Bass
species.quote: Largemouth Bass 12 inches statewide except: Lake Blackshear: 14 inches Lake Blue Ridge: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Burton: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Juliette: no minimum (0 inches) Lake Lanier: 14 inches Lake Oconee: 14 inches Lake Lindsay Grace: bass between 15 and 22 inches must be released immediately. All others may be kept. In addition, only one bass may be greater than 22 inches. Lake Walter F. George: 14 inches West Point Reservoir: 14 inches Public Fishing Area lakes operated by the Department of Natural Resources: 14 inches.
species.size: 12 inches total length statewide (lake exceptions: 14 in at Blackshear, Lanier, Oconee, Walter F. George, West Point, PFA lakes; no minimum at Blue Ridge, Burton, Juliette; Lindsay Grace protected slot 15–22)
species.limit: 10 (counts in the 10 black bass daily limit, Game Species Daily Limits page); 5 on Public Fishing Areas
species.notes: Bag from Game Species Daily Limits: 'All black bass species (Genus Micropterus). 10'. PFA page: 'Largemouth bass: 14 inches minimum unless otherwise posted.' and 'Largemouth bass (unless otherwise posted) - 5'. Per-PFA exceptions: Marben 'five (5) largemouth bass, only one (1) of which can be 16 inches or longer'; Dodge County 'between 16 and 24 inches must be released immediately ... (limit 5 total per person, only 1 over 24 inches)'; Evans County 'between 12 and 16 inches must be released immediately ... Limit five (5) per person, with only one (1) over 16 inches'; Hugh M. Gillis 'between 16 and 24 inches must be released immediately ... (limit 5 per person)'; Ocmulgee 'Largemouth bass are catch-and-release'; Paradise '5 total per person, only one over 24 inches'; Silver Lake Panic Pond 'one fish greater than 24 inches per day'.

zones.label: Georgia freshwater, statewide
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass of all species combined

zones.label: Lakes Blackshear, Lanier, Oconee, Walter F. George, West Point
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass of all species combined

zones.label: Lakes Blue Ridge, Burton, Juliette
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass of all species combined

zones.label: Lake Lindsay Grace (Wayne Co.)
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass; only one bass may be greater than 22 inches
zones.sizeNote: Bass 15–22 inches must be released; keep under 15 or over 22 (only one over 22)

zones.label: DNR Public Fishing Areas (default)
zones.bagNote: 5 per person unless otherwise posted

zones.label: GA–SC border waters (Savannah/Tugaloo/Chattooga rivers, Clarks Hill, Russell, Hartwell, Yonah, Tugaloo, Stevens Creek lakes)
zones.bagNote: 10 bass (largemouth, spotted, redeye, smallmouth or combination)

userNotes: Statewide minimum is 12 inches; it is 14 inches on Blackshear, Lanier, Oconee, Walter F. George, West Point and DNR Public Fishing Area lakes; no minimum on Blue Ridge, Burton and Juliette.
Lake Lindsay Grace: release every bass between 15 and 22 inches, and keep only one bass over 22.

Daily limit is 10 black bass of all species combined (only 5 may be the native stream species). On PFAs the limit is 5 largemouth and several PFAs have their own slots: Marben (1 over 16 in), Dodge County and Hugh M. Gillis (release 16–24 in), Evans County (release 12–16 in, 1 over 16), Paradise (1 over 24 in), Ocmulgee (catch-and-release only), Silver Lake Panic Pond (1 over 24 in).
No more than 50 game fish total of all species (except channel and flathead catfish) may be possessed.

species.name: Shoal Bass
species.quote: Shoal Bass 15-inches statewide except: Flint River downstream of Warwick Dam (Lake Blackshear): Bass between 15 and 20 inches must be released immediately. All others may be kept.
species.size: 15 inches total length statewide; Flint River below Warwick Dam: release 15–20 inches
species.limit: Part of the 10 black bass limit, only 5 of which may be Altamaha, Bartrams, Chattahoochee, Coosa, Shoal, Smallmouth, Suwannee, Tallapoosa
species.notes: Bag from Game Species Daily Limits page.

zones.label: Georgia freshwater, statewide
zones.bagNote: Within the 10 black bass limit, no more than 5 combined of shoal, Altamaha, Bartram's, Chattahoochee, Coosa, smallmouth, Suwannee, Tallapoosa bass

zones.label: Flint River downstream of Warwick Dam (Lake Blackshear)
zones.bagNote: Within the 10 black bass limit, no more than 5 of the native stream bass species
zones.sizeNote: Bass between 15 and 20 inches must be released; all others may be kept

userNotes: Shoal bass must be 15 inches statewide. On the Flint River below Warwick Dam (Lake Blackshear) you must release 15–20 inch fish and may keep fish under 15 or over 20.
Counts toward the 10-bass daily limit, and toward the sub-limit of 5 native stream bass (shoal, Altamaha, Bartram's, Chattahoochee, Coosa, smallmouth, Suwannee, Tallapoosa).

species.name: Spotted Bass
species.size: None statewide; 14 inches on Lake Lanier
species.limit: Part of the 10 black bass daily limit
species.notes: 'There are no minimum length limits on freshwater game fish unless they are listed below'. Spotted bass is not in the 5-fish native-stream sub-limit list.

zones.label: Georgia freshwater, statewide
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass of all species combined

zones.label: Lake Lanier
zones.bagNote: 10 black bass of all species combined

userNotes: No minimum size statewide, but spotted bass on Lake Lanier must be 14 inches.
Counts toward the 10 black bass daily limit.

species.name: White Bass
aliases: striped bass, white bass and/or hybrid white-striped bass
species.quote: Striped Bass, White Bass and/or Hybrid White-Striped Bass | — | 15, only two of which can be 22 inches or longer.
species.size: None (only two of the 15 may be 22 inches or longer)
species.limit: 15 combined striped, white and hybrid bass, only two of which can be 22 inches or longer
species.notes: Game Species exceptions: coastal rivers list and saltwater 'is a two fish limit, both of which must be 22 inches in length or longer'; Savannah River below J. Strom Thurmond Dam 'two fish limit, both of which must be 27 inches in length or longer'. GA–SC border: 'White bass | All border waters covered except for Savannah River downstream of Clarks Hill dam | 10 | No size limit'; 'Striped bass, hybrid bass, white bass or combination | Savannah River downstream of Clarks Hill dam | 2 | 27-inch minimum length limit'. Florida: 'The limit for striped bass, white bass, and hybrid white-striped bass on the St. Mary's River is two fish which must be 22 inches or longer.'

zones.bagNote: 15 striped, white and hybrid bass combined; only 2 may be 22 inches or longer
zones.sizeNote: No minimum; only two fish 22 inches or longer

zones.label: North Newport, Medway (incl. Mount Hope Creek), Little Ogeechee, Ogeechee, Oconee below GA 22, Ocmulgee below GA 96, Altamaha, St. Mary's, Satilla rivers and tributaries

userNotes: Statewide freshwater: 15 striped, white and hybrid bass combined, and only 2 of them may be 22 inches or longer.

In the lower coastal rivers (Ogeechee, Altamaha, Satilla, St. Mary's, lower Oconee/Ocmulgee, etc.) the limit is 2 fish and each must be at least 22 inches; on the Savannah below Thurmond Dam it is 2 fish at 27 inches.
On the GA–SC border lakes (Hartwell, Clarks Hill, Russell, etc.) white bass limit is 10 with no size limit.

species.name: Lake Sturgeon
species.quote: Coosa River: The season for taking lake sturgeon from the Coosa River and its tributaries is CLOSED.
species.notes: Game Species Daily Limits page: 'Sturgeon – May not be taken in fresh or saltwater in Georgia.'

zones.label: Georgia freshwater, statewide (incl. Coosa River)
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

userNotes: Sturgeon of any kind may not be taken in fresh or salt water in Georgia. The Coosa River lake sturgeon season is closed — release immediately.

species.name: Grass Carp
species.quote: Grass carp must be released immediately.
species.season: Possession prohibited on Public Fishing Areas
species.notes: Printed only in the Public Fishing Areas length/daily limits block; no statewide limit is printed.

zones.label: DNR Public Fishing Areas
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

userNotes: On any DNR Public Fishing Area, grass carp must be released immediately — they are stocked for weed control.
No statewide limit is printed for grass carp outside PFAs.

species.name: Whelk
species.quote: Whelk (conch) Recreational harvest of whelk is limited to 1 bushel/person. There is no minimum size, closed season or closed area. A recreational fishing license and Saltwater Information Permit (SIP) are required, including hand harvest from the beach.
species.notes: Bushel = 8 gallons (recreational fishing page definitions). Not printed on the gadnrle.org shrimpregs page — eRegulations guide only.

zones.label: GA state waters and beaches
zones.bagNote: 1 bushel per person

userNotes: Whelk (conch): 1 bushel (8 gallons) per person, no size limit, no closed season or area.
A fishing license and free Saltwater Information Permit are required even for picking whelks by hand on the beach.

species.name: Stone Crab
species.quote: Georgia does not regulate the harvest of stone crab; however, the harvest of the whole crab is discouraged. It is recommended that only one claw measuring at least 2 3⁄4 inches from the elbow to the tip of the lower, immovable finger be removed. A properly removed claw should not have meat from the body attached.
species.size: None (recommended: claw at least 2 3/4 inches elbow to tip of immovable finger)
species.notes: Unregulated; the agency prints a recommendation only (one claw, 2 3/4 inch minimum, no body meat attached). Same text on the eRegulations shrimp/crab page.

zones.label: GA state waters
zones.bagNote: No limit — unregulated
zones.sizeNote: No legal minimum; DNR recommends one claw of at least 2 3/4 inches

userNotes: Georgia does not regulate stone crab harvest, but DNR asks that you take only one claw (at least 2 3/4 inches from elbow to tip of the fixed finger) and release the crab rather than keeping the whole animal.

species.name: Bait Minnows (saltwater)
species.quote: Bait minnows may be harvested year-round. ... No individual recreationally harvesting bait minnows may possess more than two quarts of bait minnows at any given time. A licensed saltwater fishing guide may possess not more than 10 quarts at any given time.
species.limit: 2 quarts per person at any time (licensed saltwater guide: 10 quarts)
species.notes: Gear: no more than two minnow traps recreationally (guide: four); trap less than 24x18x9 in or 30 in circumference, throat no larger than 1 in, bar mesh not smaller than 1/4 in, tag/float with name and address; seines and cast nets also allowed year-round.

zones.label: GA state saltwaters
zones.bagNote: 2 quarts per person at any time (10 quarts for a licensed saltwater guide)

userNotes: You may hold no more than 2 quarts of bait minnows at a time (10 quarts for a licensed saltwater fishing guide).
Up to two minnow traps per person (four for a guide), each tagged with your name and address; cast nets and seines are also allowed year-round.

corrections.shouldBe: Add note: 'South Carolina regulations differ for crappie and bream' on GA–SC border waters; the 40-fish aggregate of all game fish applies on border waters and the 50-fish aggregate statewide.

corrections.current: state (cast net food shrimp 48 qt heads-on / 30 qt tails, seasons 06-15 to 01-15); bait (4 qt/day)
corrections.shouldBe: Add a seine zone: food shrimp by seine only — 24 quarts heads-on or 15 quarts tails per person per 24 hours (cast-net limits apply if a cast net is also aboard). Bait zone: also 2 quarts possession at any time, 4 qt/8 qt per boat when two or more aboard; bait trawl (10 ft, sport bait trawl) same 2/4 qt limits, no more than 1/2 pint dead, daylight only, only in DNR bait zones. Season window is set yearly by the Commissioner (may open May 15 – end of February; generally mid-June to mid-January) — the hard-coded 06-15 to 01-15 should be flagged as approximate.
corrections.quote: No one person taking food shrimp solely by means of a seine, whether such person is acting alone or in a group of persons, may possess more than 24 quarts of shrimp with heads on or 15 quarts of tails taken by such seine in any 24-hour period.

corrections.shouldBe: Add: 'No sponge (egg-bearing) crabs are allowed.' Mature adult females and peelers (3 in) exempt from the 5-inch minimum. Crab traps may only be set in waters defined as saltwater (St. Mary's and Satilla seaward of the Seaboard Coastline Railroad; Altamaha system seaward of I-95).
corrections.quote: It is unlawful to take or possess any crab less than 5 inches from spike to spike across the back (other than a “peeler” or a “mature adult female” crab). Peelers must measure at least 3 inches from spike to spike across the back. No sponge (egg-bearing) crabs are allowed.

corrections.current: State waters only; federal waters (3–200 mi) have a separate, very short season — see safmc.net.
corrections.shouldBe: Also add for Amberjack, Black Sea Bass, Dolphin, Gag Grouper, King Mackerel, Red Porgy, Spanish Mackerel and Red Snapper: 'Effective Jan. 1, 2027 a Reef & Migratory Fish Endorsement ($10 resident / $20 non-resident) is required to land this species in Georgia.' and the federal link printed by CRD (e.g. https://safmc.net/species/snapper-red/).
corrections.quote: Effective January 1, 2027, a “Reef & Migratory Fish Endorsement” will be required of any angler landing any of the following nine species in Georgia: Amberjack, Black sea bass, Cobia, Dolphin, Gag, King Mackerel, Red Porgy, Red Snapper, and Spanish Mackerel.

corrections.shouldBe: Add the Jan. 1, 2027 Reef & Migratory Fish Endorsement note (cobia is one of the nine species).
corrections.quote: Effective January 1, 2027, a “Reef & Migratory Fish Endorsement” will be required of any angler landing any of the following nine species in Georgia: Amberjack, Black sea bass, Cobia, Dolphin, Gag, King Mackerel, Red Porgy, Red Snapper, and Spanish Mackerel.

corrections.shouldBe: Add gear note: only flounder may be taken with a gig; all size and bag limits apply regardless of gear.
corrections.quote: Only flounder may be taken with a gig (any handheld shaft with single or multiple points, barbed or barbless).

corrections.shouldBe: Add explicit state and federal zones with closed: true, bagNote 'Possession prohibited', and note that no sturgeon may be taken in fresh or salt water.
corrections.quote: Sturgeon – May not be taken in fresh or saltwater in Georgia.

issues: https://coastalgadnr.org/ShellfishHarvest returned 'Page not found'; the equivalent CRD page is https://coastalgadnr.org/Shellfish/Recreational (reached via the CoastalGADNR.org/ApprovedRecHarvestAreas redirect) and was used instead.

Official sources conflict for Bluefish season (CRD: 'May 1 - Feb. 28 annually'; eRegulations: 'All year') and Gag Grouper minimum size (CRD: 25" TL; eRegulations: 24 TL). Both filed as corrections flagged for confirmation; no value was chosen from memory.
The CRD limits page does not print a Hammerhead row at all (eRegulations prints 78 FL). The Hammerhead row added here uses the eRegulations text.

The eRegulations shark rows merge the limit cell ('1 per angler or boat, whichever is less') across Sharks (other), Hammerheads and Shortfin Mako; the hammerhead and mako rows added here inherit that limit from the merged cell.

Food-shrimp season dates are set annually by the DNR Commissioner and announced by CRD; the existing hard-coded 06-15 to 01-15 window is only the 'generally' wording from the regulation and should be treated as approximate.
Federal SAFMC and NOAA HMS pages were not fetched (out of scope: not state sources); the state's printed links are recorded in notes/userNotes instead.
No official page prints a limit for Southern Kingfish (whiting), tunas or swordfish; these were not added.
